speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand what is going on, can you tell me exactly where the wrist pain is located and describe the appearance of the skin lesions? Also, have you measured your temperature, and if so, how high has the fever been?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Do you recall any specific insect bites, particularly ticks, during your camping trip in Minnesota? Additionally, have you noticed any skin lesions that look like a "bull's-eye" rash, and are you currently experiencing any joint swelling or redness in the affected wrist?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: The painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on your hands and wrists are a very specific sign. Have you recently been exposed to warm water springs or lakes, and do you have any history of psoriasis or other autoimmune conditions?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. Social history: Admits to being sexually active with one female partner who uses a diaphragm for contraception. Recently went on a camping trip to Minnesota.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the camping history in Minnesota and the specific skin lesions, I need to rule out Spotted Fever Group rickettsiosis. Have you noticed any other rash appearing on your wrists, ankles, or palms, and did you experience a headache or nausea before the joint pain started?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies trauma to the wrist, reports a history of knee pain that resolved on its own. No other systemic symptoms mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The combination of migratory arthritis, fever, and painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the hands and wrists after exposure to fresh water in Minnesota is highly characteristic of Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae infection, also known as Erysipeloid. I will request blood cultures and a Gram stain of the lesion to confirm the diagnosis.
